newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Bonos closed higher on a bout of short-covering in thin volume, dealers said.

The market was bracing for a wave of profit-taking even though the general trend is expected to remain positive, traders added. Any dip could be seen as a good buying opportunity, they said. The steepening of the yield curve is likely to continue.

"The differential between the three and 10-year was 90 bp and is now around 110. It could go higher," a dealer said. The 10-year bond rose to 106.86 from 106.39 at Friday's close, yielding 7.75 percent. The three-year 7.8 percent bond rose to 102.74 from 102.23, yielding 6.66 percent.
The mood toward peripheral markets remained positive, buoyed by optimism on European convergence.

"The Spanish market is not yet completely discounting Spain entering in the EMU from its start," said Carmen Nuzzo, a London-based analyst at Salomon Brothers. She forecast a spread over 10-year bunds at 100 basis points by the end of 1997.
On Monday, that spread slimmed to 173 from 182 on Friday.
The Spanish peseta firmed with the mark weaker and the Italian lira was also stronger. The peseta closed around 84.09/10 versus the mark from 84.14/16.
